skill.name: plate-handler
skill.description: Build Plate.js rich text editors for React apps, from small comment fields to detailed document and CMS editors.
skill.summary: Guides Plate.js editor setup, plugin selection, toolbar configuration, and content state handling.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed the install instructions that run pnpm dlx shadcn@latest, which executes a remote CLI and modifies project files. Other backtick detections are markdown references to components or paths, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin shadcn and package versions where possible, and require explicit user approval before running pnpm dlx commands.
Document the expected files and dependencies changed by each command so users can review the impact before execution.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent rich text editors without wiring Plate.js plugins from scratch. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through setup and implementation.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Plate.js install commands for core editor and basic node packages.
Distinguishes small comment editors from full document or CMS editors.
Outlines plugin choices for marks, headings, blockquotes, lists, images, media, and tables.
Shows where to place simple and detailed editor components in a React project.
Explains state handling with Plate value and onChange for storage or forms.
limitations: It does not provide a packaged runtime component or npm library.
It assumes a React project that can use Plate.js, shadcn UI, Tailwind, and Radix.
The CLI examples may change project files and need user approval.
Examples need adaptation for authentication, validation, and production storage.

use_cases.title: Add a Comment Editor
use_cases.description: Build a compact editor with basic marks for comments, chat, or profile fields.

use_cases.title: Create CMS Editing Fields
use_cases.description: Implement a larger editor with headings, blockquotes, lists, media, and structured content storage.

use_cases.title: Standardize Rich Text Setup
use_cases.description: Give teams a repeatable Plate.js setup path for shadcn-based React applications.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Editor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to create a small Plate.js editor for comments with bold, italic, underline, and a minimal toolbar.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Blog Editor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to build a detailed Plate.js editor for blog posts with headings, blockquotes, lists, and persistent form state.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Existing Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to add Plate.js editing to my existing shadcn UI form. Match current component paths and toolbar style.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Plate Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use plate-handler to review my Plate.js editor setup for plugin configuration, state handling, and safe rendering practices.

output_examples.input: A request for a comment editor in a Next.js app.
output_examples.output: A plan for a small Plate.js editor, required shadcn components, plugin list, component path, and storage notes.

output_examples.input: A request for a blog editor with headings and quotes.
output_examples.output: A detailed editor design with recommended Plate plugins, toolbar groups, component locations, and state management guidance.

output_examples.input: A request to make saved rich text safer.
output_examples.output: Guidance to store Plate value data, avoid direct HTML injection, and serialize only for trusted read-only rendering.

best_practices: Pin or review CLI package versions before running installation commands.
Use Plate value and onChange for saved content instead of storing rendered HTML.
Choose the smallest plugin set that matches the user workflow.
anti_patterns: Running package installation commands without user confirmation.
Adding full document plugins to short chat or comment fields.

faq.question: Does this skill install Plate.js automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides CLI guidance, and the user or agent must approve commands in the project.

faq.question: Can it build simple and detailed editors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers small comment editors and larger document or CMS editors.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe to store editor content as HTML?
faq.answer: The skill recommends storing Plate value data and serializing HTML only for trusted read-only rendering.

faq.question: Which framework does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes a React project using Plate.js and shadcn UI components.

faq.question: Can it work with existing shadcn components?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides placement and reuse of editor, toolbar, and node components in existing projects.
